name: Time limit for issuing a tax invoice
definition: Rule 47 fixes when a tax invoice for a taxable supply of SERVICES must be issued: within thirty days of the supply, forty five days for insurers, banking companies and financial institutions, and, for specified suppliers making supplies between distinct persons, by the end of the quarter.
why_it_exists: An invoice date that sits outside the permitted window is a defect visible from the document alone, without any accounting judgement. It is one of the few checks a machine can make with certainty.
inputs: the date of the supply of service
whether the supply is between distinct persons under section 25
preconditions: the supply is a taxable supply of services
the date of supply of service is known
exceptions: insurers, banking companies and financial institutions including non-banking financial companies have forty five days
specified suppliers making supplies between distinct persons may invoice by the end of the quarter
common_mistakes: applying the thirty-day limit to a supply of goods — rule 47 says 'in the case of the taxable supply of services'
measuring from the invoice date instead of the date of supply of service
applying the forty five day period to any large company — it is limited to insurers, banking companies and financial institutions
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — a statutory invoicing deadline is not an accounting standard question
gst_references: UNKNOWN — the time limit for issuing an invoice for a supply of GOODS is fixed by section 31 of the CGST Act, a different document not read for this record
UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the date of supply of service
confidence_factors: weak when the date of supply of service is not on the document
weak when it is unclear whether the supply is of goods or of services, because rule 47 only reaches services
validation_checks: invoice date minus date of supply of service is at most 30 days for an ordinary supplier of services
at most 45 days where the supplier is an insurer, banking company or financial institution
no arithmetic check is performed where the supply is of goods, because rule 47 does not govern it
examples: service supplied 1 April, invoice dated 25 April, ordinary supplier — within the thirty days
counterexamples: service supplied 1 April, invoice dated 15 May, ordinary supplier — outside thirty days
goods delivered 1 April, invoice dated 15 May — rule 47 says nothing about this; do not report it as late on the strength of rule 47

evidence.quote: 47. Time limit for issuing tax invoice.- The invoice referred to in rule 46, in the case of the taxable supply of services, shall be issued within a period of thirty days from the date of the supply of service:
the period within which the invoice or any document in lieu thereof is to be issued shall be forty five days from the date of the supply of service:
